subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default for interactive browser tasks, and what explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain?
rationale: Current main has caps, efficient mode, compact role snapshots, and compact action responses, but changing the default model-facing browser contract affects ref completeness and existing automation behavior.

options.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
options.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable while preserving explicit full AI/ARIA reads for complete page-state workflows.

options.title: Keep efficient mode opt-in
options.body: Leave defaults unchanged and rely on documented mode=efficient, maxChars, selector reads, and generic truncation for context-heavy workflows.

options.title: Fold into browser field report
options.body: Track this under the broader browser automation field report if maintainers want one umbrella for action diffs, stale refs, viewport reads, and context shaping.

recommendation.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
recommendation.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable while preserving explicit full AI/ARIA reads for complete page-state workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal across browser snapshot/control design and plugin extraction.
